extracted.intended_audience: Members of Parliament and the politically engaged British public concerned with East India Company governance
extracted.subtask_description: A parliamentary/oratorical critique of East India Company financial practices in the Carnatic, arguing standards for legitimate public payment, inquiry, and governance. The text sets out normative principles for how ministers, courts, creditors, and Company servants should behave and be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not divert territorial revenues so troops go unpaid
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire revenue of those districts is by your Highness's order set apart to discharge the tunkaws granted to the Europeans... your Highness's troops have seven or eight months' pay due, which they cannot receive, and are thereby reduced to the greatest distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assigning district revenues to private assignments (tunkaws) that cause garrisons or public troops to miss pay and thereby induce mutiny; recognise bond-paid-by-bond chains that convert arrears into new arrears and destabilize defence and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require proper inquiry before authorizing payment of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: They have ordered the payment of the whole mass of these unknown, unliquidated sums, without an attempt to ascertain them... without any sort of inquiry into its authenticity,—without a single step taken to settle even the amount of the demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministers must follow prescribed inquiry procedures before approving large public payments: verify authenticity, amount, and rightful proprietors; do not authorize broad settlements without documentary and investigative foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place the burden of proof on claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: "To put the burden of the proof on those who make the demand?... You say, you have a demand of some millions ... prove that you have acted by lawful authority; prove, at least, that your money has been bonâ fide advanced."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require claimants to demonstrate lawful authority and bona fide advance of funds before granting state protection or payment; an honest creditor should accept such a test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish fraudulent from bona fide claims through active discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: By taking, in this arrangement, no measures for discrimination and discovery, the fraudulent and the fair are in the first instance confounded in one mass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should implement procedures for discriminating valid claims from collusive or fictitious ones (audits, documentary proofs, local inquiries), rather than establishing all claims en masse and leaving post facto selection to interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on biased local courts or conflicted adjudicators
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mayor's Court!... the members of that court were themselves creditors, and therefore could not sit as judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure adjudicative bodies are impartial and free from conflicts of interest; recognize that local courts populated by creditors cannot be trusted to deliver fair justice on creditor claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid retroactive capitalization and excessive compound interest on public debt
rubrics_metrics.description: They have added the arrear of twelve per cent interest... raising thereby 160 to 294,000 l. Then they charge a new twelve per cent on the whole from that period... added the whole growth of four years' usury of twelve per cent to the first overgrown principal; and has again grafted on this meliorated stock a perpetual annuity of six per cent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expand questionable claims by compounding interest or grafting perpetual annuities that transform disputed sums into vast, effectively unassailable public liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require identification and listing of proprietors before payment
rubrics_metrics.description: —without an attempt so much as to ascertain the real persons claiming a sum ... —without an attempt made to ascertain the proprietors, of whom no list has ever yet been laid before the Court of Directors,—of proprietors who are known to be in a collusive shuffle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments should be preceded by transparent lists of claimants/proprietors; absence of such lists or evidence of collusive reshuffling is a ground for withholding payment and initiating investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not immunize specific loans from litigation or exception
rubrics_metrics.description: He complained of unfair dealing in the Cavalry Loan. It is fixed upon him with interest on interest; and this loan is excepted from all power of litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating categories of debt or loans that are shielded from legal challenge; permitting exceptions undermines accountability and invites abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat changes in ministers' stated motives as suspicious
rubrics_metrics.description: It is one of the known indications of guilt to stagger and prevaricate in a story... His dispatch assigns motives of policy, concord, trade, and circulation: his speech proclaims discord and litigations, and proposes, as the ultimate end, detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inconsistency between official dispatches and public speeches, or shifting rationales for decisions, should trigger scrutiny as potential signs of collusion or bad faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult broad sources, not only agents of claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: So perfectly has his conduct confounded his understanding, that he fairly tells you that through the course of the whole business he has never conferred with any but the agents of the pretended creditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers must consult a wide range of parties (local authorities, native claimants, independent investigators), not only agents representing alleged creditors, to avoid captured or one-sided decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize justice for native, bonâ fide creditors and victims
rubrics_metrics.description: The creditors most certainly not fraudulent are the natives... They lent bonâ fide... these unhappy natives are deprived of every hope of payment for their real debts, to make provision for the arrears of unsatisfied bribery and treason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precedence to indigenous or vulnerable creditors who lent in good faith and suffered loss; avoid privileging politically connected European creditors at the natives' expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require legal authority and public-purpose for bond-contracted debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the legal authority on which this debt was contracted, of its purposes for the very being of the state, of its publicity and fairness, no doubt has been entertained for a moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept only debts contracted with proper legal authority, for bona fide public purposes, and with adequate publicity and fairness; reject or investigate bonds lacking these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government must restore and maintain the population and infrastructure before extracting revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: "The road to economy lies not through receipt, but through expense; and in that country Nature has given no short cut to your object. Men must propagate, like other animals, by the mouth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic recovery requires public investment (relief, maintenance of irrigation, seed and stock) rather than immediate extraction; do not treat devastated territories as ready sources of revenue without first nursing population and productive capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and account for essential local infrastructure (reservoirs, watercourses) when planning revenue assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Carnatic... its product of rice exacts the use of water subject to perpetual command... a number... of reservoirs have been made... they are formed... and maintained at a mighty charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning or estimating revenue from an agrarian territory, account for the maintenance costs and necessity of irrigation works and other infrastructure; stripping these resources to pay creditors destroys productive capacity and future revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be suspicious of financial contrivances that allow insiders to 'soucaring' or mortgage provinces
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole art and mystery, the true free-mason secret, of the profession of soucaring... innocent, inexperienced young Englishmen... are enabled at once to take provinces in mortgage, to make princes their debtors, and to become creditors for millions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and guard against informal financial practices and contrivances (private notes, banker arrangements, tunkaws) that enable insiders to capture territory and revenues without bona fide advances or legal basis.
